properties.srs_summary:
Document: Software Requirements Specification — ShobarKhamar Android Application
Functional requirements summary:
- Authentication (FR-AUTH-01 to 07): Session is pre-established; registration, OTP, password recovery, and account deletion are out of scope. Assume signed-in state persists across restarts.
- Navigation & Discovery (FR-NAV-01 to 08): Splash screen, primary nav (Home, Blog, Order, Search, Menu), home entry points for Cattle/Feed/Medicine/Equipment/Farmer Market, search, detail views, pagination/lazy loading, loading/empty/failure states, location selector in header.
- Product Browsing (FR-PROD-01 to 08): Browse cattle, feed, medicine, equipment based on role. Detail view shows price/description/seller. Share via device sheet. Filters by category/type/breed/price/location. Unavailable products show status, not broken views.
- Favourites (FR-FAV-01 to 05): Add/remove products from favourites with visible acknowledgement. List reflects current state. State persists when leaving/re-entering detail view.
- Order Requests (FR-ORD-01 to 12): Buyers initiate requests with required info; success/failure feedback. Buyer sees order list/detail/status updates. Sellers (cattle/feed/medicine/machinery) view incoming orders and update status. Empty lists show clear state. Errors surface visibly. Duplicate submissions prevented.
- Farm & Animal Management (FR-FARM-01 to 06, FR-ANM-01 to 04): Seller registers farm (name, type, animal category, location via map/device). Mandatory fields validated. Updates produce feedback. Multi-step animal addition supports type/sub-type/breed; abandoning midway prevents partial records.
- Seller Publishing (FR-SELL-01 to 14): Publish/edit listings (cattle, feed, medicine, machinery) with images from gallery/camera. Validate inputs. Change availability. Listings appear in buyer marketplace. Role isolation enforced (sellers see only own listings/orders; cannot access other roles' screens).
- Reviews (FR-REV-01 to 07): View seller reviews/ratings. Submit review after eligible interaction with validation. Success acknowledged. Pagination supported. No-review state shows empty state, not error.
- Chat (FR-CHT-01 to 05): Inbox lists conversations. Message history ordered. Send messages with immediate appearance. Empty inbox shows empty state.
- Notifications (FR-NOT-01 to 05): List notifications, display unread count, mark read (updating count). Empty state shown if none. Deep links open referenced content.
- Location (FR-LOC-01 to 06): Request permission when needed. Rank nearby farms/products. Select/confirm location on map. Denying permission keeps non-location features usable. Prevent concurrent duplicate requests. Changing region updates discovery.
- Disease & Health Check (FR-DIS-01 to 05): Browse disease list/details (symptoms/prevention/remedy). AI health check accepts image for inference. Result presented with limitations. Failures produce errors, not blanks.
- Profile & Settings (FR-PROF-01 to 04, FR-SET-01 to 02): Display/edit/persist profile fields. Shareable link. Settings per role. Sign-out ends session (out of scope due to OTP requirement).

Non-functional requirements summary:
- NFR-01: Primary screens interactive without unreasonable delay on stable network.
- NFR-02: Long lists use pagination; no unbounded loads.
- NFR-03: Network/image/inference work does not block UI.
- NFR-04: Backend failures reported to user, not silent.
- NFR-05: Interface usable offline or on slow networks.
- NFR-06: Destructive/irreversible actions require explicit confirmation.

Validation and constraints:
- PRECONDITION-SATISFIED: Do not test FR-AUTH-01 through FR-AUTH-06. Assume authenticated session.
- Out of Scope: Password recovery/change (FR-AUTH-05), Account deletion (FR-AUTH-06), Sign-out (FR-SET-02).
- Media Note: For FR-SELL-01, FR-SELL-14, FR-DIS-03, use pre-seeded gallery images instead of camera capture.
- Role Dependency: Medicine/Equipment browsing and publishing depend on specific seller roles being active/approved.
- Data Integrity: Ensure favourite state persistence, prevent duplicate orders, prevent partial animal records on abandonment.

Coverage priorities for next tests:
- High Priority: Order lifecycle end-to-end (Buyer request -> Seller status update -> Buyer visibility) including duplicate prevention (FR-ORD-12) and error handling (FR-ORD-11).
- High Priority: Seller role isolation and data visibility (FR-SELL-12, FR-SELL-13) to ensure cross-role leakage does not occur.
- High Priority: Validation logic for mandatory fields in Farm Registration (FR-FARM-04) and Listing Submission (FR-SELL-05).
- Medium Priority: Favourites persistence across navigation (FR-FAV-05) and visual feedback (FR-FAV-04).
- Medium Priority: Location-based filtering accuracy and graceful degradation when permissions are denied (FR-LOC-04, FR-LOC-06).
- Medium Priority: AI Health Check failure states and result disclaimers (FR-DIS-04, FR-DIS-05).
- Low Priority: Review submission validation and pagination (FR-REV-04, FR-REV-06).
- Non-Functional Focus: Verify UI responsiveness during heavy network operations (NFR-03) and offline usability (NFR-05).

properties.generation_prompt:
You are a world-class EXPLORATORY software tester running an adaptive, session-based testing charter on Shobar Khamar.
Session objective: generate next high-value non-duplicate test case

## Exploratory testing mindset — apply throughout
- This is EXPLORATORY testing, NOT scripted regression: continuously learn from the SRS, the UI, and prior results, then steer toward where undiscovered defects most likely hide.
- Your mission is to DISCOVER BUGS, not to confirm expected behaviour.
- Test adversarially: simultaneously design, execute (in intent), and learn — each test should be the single highest-information probe for THIS moment in the session.
- Stay strictly app-agnostic: rely ONLY on the SRS, UI, and history context provided below. Never assume features, screens, or rules that are not evidenced in that context.
- Generate exactly ONE test case optimised to uncover a defect not yet found.

## Live Coverage State
No tests executed yet — start of exploration session. Begin with broad coverage.

## Exploration Directive — follow this priority order
[OPEN EXPLORATION] No specific signal. Aim for breadth first, then depth.

## Session Constraints — these override every other instruction
- The device is already signed in as a 'farmer/seller'. Generate tests reachable by that role; do not assume permissions it lacks. Current account state: This seller account is fully set up: it already has a registered farm ("Trust Dairy Farm") with products listed, and the app language is already English. Farm registration, store registration and language selection are therefore already done. Do NOT write a test that requires creating something this account already has — there is no entry point for it and the test cannot run. Test changing, viewing or validating what exists instead.
- The following areas are OUT OF SCOPE. Never generate a test whose steps or preconditions require them, even when the requirements below describe them and even when they look untested:
    - account registration
    - OTP verification
    - password reset
    - password change
    - account deletion
    - sign out
    - NID document upload
    - seller account approval
    - FR-AUTH
  They are excluded because completing them needs something outside the agent's control (an SMS code, an identity document, an admin approval, or a phone number that is spent on first use) — not because they are unimportant. Treat them as already satisfied and test what they unlock.

## Deriving Expected Behavior (no SRS/requirements available)
No formal requirements were provided. Derive expected behavior from the UI affordances below and universal UX/robustness expectations: inputs are validated, every action gives feedback, navigation is reversible, state survives interruption, and the app never crashes or loses data. A violation of these is a bug. Leave 'requirement_ids' empty ([]).

## Executed Tests — semantic duplicates are FORBIDDEN
- none

## Known Failures — probe adjacent cases and variants around these
- none

## Exploratory Testing Heuristics — apply at least one
- BOUNDARY: Test at the edges of valid input ranges (max length, empty, zero, one-off, overflow).
- INVALID INPUT: Submit malformed, null, or unexpected-type data. Does the app fail gracefully?
- STATE TRANSITION: Perform an action and verify the app reaches the correct subsequent state.
- INTERRUPTION: Start an action, navigate away mid-flow, then return — is data/state preserved?
- COMBINATION: Test interactions between two features that may have unexpected side-effects.
- RECOVERY: After an error or warning, can the user correct and retry without restarting?
- PERMISSION / ACCESS: Test behaviours requiring specific preconditions or data to be present.

## Strict Decision Policy
1. FORBIDDEN: Any test semantically similar to a title in the executed list above.
2. PRIORITY: Follow the Exploration Directive — hot spots > new areas > breadth > exhausted areas.
3. PREFER negative, boundary, and state-transition tests over happy-path positive tests.
4. 'screen_hint' is a LEAD for the executor, not a command. Name the screen you believe is relevant, preferring a real observed name from the context above — but you cannot see the live app, so the executor will verify it and adapt if reality differs. 'objective' MUST state WHAT to verify in plain language (the behaviour or rule under test), NEVER a numbered sequence of taps or clicks — you do not know the exact UI well enough to script it, and a wrong literal instruction is worse than a clear goal. The executor has live access to the real app and will work out how to get there.
5. The 'rationale' field MUST name the specific defect class or risk this test is designed to expose.
5b. 'preconditions' MUST be things the tester can CREATE through the UI in this test's own first steps. NEVER state an environmental assumption the tester can only observe and not establish — the absence of data, data held on another device or account, or a state reached outside this app. If your test needs data to exist, the FIRST STEPS must create it through the UI. A test that depends on an unachievable precondition is abandoned without testing anything, which is worse than no test at all.
6. The 'area' field MUST align with the Exploration Directive — do not default to the easiest area.
7. 'requirement_ids' MUST contain ids copied EXACTLY from the '## Requirements You May Cite' list above. Never invent an id or guess a format. Use [] if none apply.
8. SELF-CONTAINED: assume the app starts EMPTY with no pre-existing data. If the test needs data (an existing record, a populated list), the FIRST steps MUST create it through the UI. Never write a precondition that merely asserts data already exists — the executor cannot conjure it and the run will abort without testing anything. 'preconditions' is for app state you can reach by navigating (e.g. 'app is open'), not for data you did not create.

## Output — STRICT JSON only. No markdown fences, no text outside the JSON object.
{"test_case_id":"...","title":"...","screen_hint":"...","preconditions":[...],"objective":"...","expected_result":"...","priority":"high|medium|low","area":"...","test_type":"positive|negative|boundary|state_transition|recovery|combination","requirement_ids":["<id copied from the list above>"],"rationale":"what specific bug or risk this test is designed to expose"}

Software Requirements Specification — ShobarKhamar Android Application
Package: com.tirzokpvt.shobarkhamar   Framework: Flutter   Build under test: 2.1.3

ShobarKhamar is a livestock and agricultural marketplace connecting farmers, buyers,
cattle sellers, feed sellers and supporting services. Users discover cattle, feed,
medicine and equipment; sellers publish listings and manage incoming order requests;
buyers favourite products, request orders, review sellers and chat with them. The app
also provides livestock disease information with AI-assisted health checking, and uses
device location to rank nearby farms and products.

SCOPE NOTE FOR THIS TEST CAMPAIGN
The device is signed in with a pre-provisioned account before the campaign starts.
Sections marked PRECONDITION-SATISFIED below describe behaviour that is already in
place and MUST NOT be re-tested: completing them requires an SMS one-time password
delivered to a phone we do not control, a national identity document, platform admin
approval, or a phone number that is consumed permanently on first use. They are listed
so their outcomes can be relied upon, not so they can be exercised. Every other section
is in scope.

1. AUTHENTICATION AND ACCOUNT STATE  [PRECONDITION-SATISFIED — do not test]
FR-AUTH-01 An account exists and is registered. Registration is not re-tested.
FR-AUTH-02 The account is signed in with a phone number and password before testing begins.
FR-AUTH-03 The account's role is already selected and, for seller roles, already approved.
FR-AUTH-04 One-time password verification has already been completed for this account.
FR-AUTH-05 Password recovery and password change are not exercised; either would lock
           the campaign out of the account it depends on.
FR-AUTH-06 Account deletion is not exercised; it would destroy the account under test.
FR-AUTH-07 The signed-in session persists across app restarts, so tests may assume an
           authenticated session at all times.

2. NAVIGATION AND DISCOVERY
FR-NAV-01 A splash screen is shown before the application becomes interactive.
FR-NAV-02 A primary navigation bar exposes Home, Blog, Order, Search and Menu.
FR-NAV-03 The home screen presents discovery entry points: Browse Cattle, Sell Cow,
          Feed, Medicine, Equipment and Farmer Market.
FR-NAV-04 A search entry point accepts free text for livestock, farms and feed.
FR-NAV-05 Product, farm and store detail views open from any discovery card or list row.
FR-NAV-06 Lists that can return more results support pagination or lazy loading.
FR-NAV-07 Remote data retrieval presents readable loading, empty and failure states.
FR-NAV-08 A location selector in the header sets the active region for discovery.

3. PRODUCT AND MARKETPLACE BROWSING
FR-PROD-01 Cattle listings are browsable with their attributes and imagery.
FR-PROD-02 Feed products are browsable by type and brand.
FR-PROD-03 Medicine and veterinary items are browsable where the role is enabled.
FR-PROD-04 Equipment items are browsable where the role is enabled.
FR-PROD-05 Product detail shows price, description, attributes and seller identity.
FR-PROD-06 Product and seller content can be shared through the device share sheet.
FR-PROD-07 Filters narrow results by category, type, breed, price and location.
FR-PROD-08 A product that is unavailable or withdrawn is presented as such rather than
           opening a broken detail view.

4. FAVOURITES
FR-FAV-01 A signed-in user adds a marketplace product to favourites.
FR-FAV-02 A signed-in user removes a product from favourites.
FR-FAV-03 The favourites list shows exactly the products currently favourited.
FR-FAV-04 Adding to favourites produces a visible acknowledgement.
FR-FAV-05 Favourite state survives leaving and re-entering the product detail view.

5. ORDER REQUESTS
FR-ORD-01 A buyer initiates an order request for an eligible product.
FR-ORD-02 The order form captures the information the backend requires.
FR-ORD-03 Submitting produces an explicit success or failure outcome.
FR-ORD-04 The buyer's order list shows their submitted order requests.
FR-ORD-05 Order detail shows status, product and seller information.
FR-ORD-06 A seller views incoming order requests for their own listings.
FR-ORD-07 A seller opens order detail and updates status to a supported value.
FR-ORD-08 The buyer sees the updated status after the seller changes it.
FR-ORD-09 Feed sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-09a Medicine sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-09b Machinery/equipment sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-10 An empty order list, or a filter matching nothing, shows a clear empty state.
FR-ORD-11 Failures in order retrieval, creation or status update surface an error.
FR-ORD-12 Submitting the same order twice does not silently create duplicates.

6. FARM AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT  (seller roles)
FR-FARM-01 A seller registers farm information including name and farm type.
FR-FARM-02 Farm registration captures animal type or category where required.
FR-FARM-03 Farm location is set from device location or a map picker.
FR-FARM-04 Mandatory farm fields are validated, and missing ones are named specifically.
FR-FARM-05 A farm owner updates farm information after registration.
FR-FARM-06 Successful and failed farm updates both produce meaningful feedback.
FR-ANM-01 A seller adds an animal record through a multi-step flow.
FR-ANM-02 The flow supports cattle type, sub-type and breed selection.
FR-ANM-03 Additional animal attributes are captured and shown on the listing.
FR-ANM-04 Abandoning the multi-step flow midway does not create a partial record.

7. SELLER STORE AND PRODUCT PUBLISHING  (cattle / feed / medicine / machinery sellers)
FR-SELL-01 A seller publishes a cattle listing with price, attributes and images.
FR-SELL-02 A seller edits an existing listing.
FR-SELL-03 A seller changes a listing's availability status.
FR-SELL-04 A feed seller registers a feed store and publishes feed products.
FR-SELL-05 Listing input is validated before submission, naming invalid fields.
FR-SELL-06 A published listing appears in the buyer-facing marketplace.
FR-SELL-07 A feed seller edits feed product details and availability.
FR-SELL-08 A medicine seller registers a store and publishes veterinary medicine items.
FR-SELL-09 A medicine seller edits a medicine item and changes its availability.
FR-SELL-10 A machinery/equipment seller registers a store and publishes equipment items.
FR-SELL-11 A machinery/equipment seller edits an equipment item and changes its availability.
FR-SELL-12 Each seller role sees only its own listings and its own incoming orders.
FR-SELL-13 A seller role cannot reach another role's publishing or order screens.
FR-SELL-14 Listing images are attachable from the device gallery or camera where the
           product type supports imagery.

8. REVIEWS AND SELLER TRUST
FR-REV-01 Seller reviews are viewable from a seller profile.
FR-REV-02 A seller rating summary is shown where ratings exist.
FR-REV-03 A buyer submits a review for a seller after an eligible interaction.
FR-REV-04 Review input is validated before submission.
FR-REV-05 Successful review submission is acknowledged and the review appears.
FR-REV-06 Review lists paginate where more reviews exist.
FR-REV-07 A seller with no reviews shows an empty state, not an error.

9. CHAT
FR-CHT-01 A chat inbox lists existing conversations.
FR-CHT-02 A conversation shows message history in order.
FR-CHT-03 A user sends a message to a seller or farmer.
FR-CHT-04 A sent message appears in the conversation immediately.
FR-CHT-05 An empty inbox shows an empty state rather than a failure.

10. NOTIFICATIONS
FR-NOT-01 A notification list shows received notifications.
FR-NOT-02 An unread count is displayed and reflects unread notifications.
FR-NOT-03 Notifications are marked read, and the unread count updates.
FR-NOT-04 An empty notification list shows an empty state.
FR-NOT-05 Supported notification deep links open the referenced content.

11. LOCATION
FR-LOC-01 Location permission is requested when a feature needs device location.
FR-LOC-02 Nearby filtering ranks farms and products by proximity when permitted.
FR-LOC-03 The current device location can be selected or confirmed on a map.
FR-LOC-04 Denying location permission leaves non-location functionality usable.
FR-LOC-05 Concurrent duplicate location requests are prevented.
FR-LOC-06 Changing the active region updates discovery results accordingly.

MEDIA NOTE
Requirements FR-SELL-01, FR-SELL-14 and FR-DIS-03 require attaching an image. Test
images are pre-seeded in the device gallery, so these flows are IN SCOPE: pick an
existing image rather than expecting the camera to produce one.

12. DISEASE INFORMATION AND HEALTH CHECK
FR-DIS-01 A list of common livestock diseases is browsable.
FR-DIS-02 Disease detail presents symptoms, prevention and remedy information.
FR-DIS-03 An AI-assisted health check accepts an image for disease inference.
FR-DIS-04 An inference result is presented with its limitations made clear.
FR-DIS-05 A failed or unavailable inference produces an error, not a blank result.

13. PROFILE AND SETTINGS
FR-PROF-01 The signed-in user's profile is displayed.
FR-PROF-02 Supported profile fields are editable and persist after saving.
FR-PROF-03 A seller profile is viewable by buyers and by the seller themselves.
FR-PROF-04 A profile can be shared via a shareable link.
FR-SET-01 Settings expose the options supported for the signed-in role.
FR-SET-02 Signing out ends the session and returns to an unauthenticated state.
           (Do not exercise: signing out requires OTP to sign back in.)

14. NON-FUNCTIONAL
NFR-01 Primary screens become interactive without unreasonable delay on a stable network.
NFR-02 Long lists paginate rather than loading unbounded result sets.
NFR-03 Network, image and inference work does not block the interface.
NFR-04 Backend failures are reported to the user rather than failing silently.
NFR-05 The interface remains usable when the device is offline or the network is slow.
NFR-06 Destructive or irreversible actions require explicit confirmation.

## Exploratory Testing Heuristics — apply at least one
- BOUNDARY: Test at the edges of valid input ranges (max length, empty, zero, one-off, overflow).
- INVALID INPUT: Submit malformed, null, or unexpected-type data. Does the app fail gracefully?
- STATE TRANSITION: Perform an action and verify the app reaches the correct subsequent state.
- INTERRUPTION: Start an action, navigate away mid-flow, then return — is data/state preserved?
- COMBINATION: Test interactions between two features that may have unexpected side-effects.
- RECOVERY: After an error or warning, can the user correct and retry without restarting?
- PERMISSION / ACCESS: Test behaviours requiring specific preconditions or data to be present.

## Strict Decision Policy
1. FORBIDDEN: Any test semantically similar to a title in the executed list above.
2. PRIORITY: Follow the Exploration Directive — hot spots > new areas > breadth > exhausted areas.
3. PREFER negative, boundary, and state-transition tests over happy-path positive tests.
4. 'screen_hint' is a LEAD for the executor, not a command. Name the screen you believe is relevant, preferring a real observed name from the context above — but you cannot see the live app, so the executor will verify it and adapt if reality differs. 'objective' MUST state WHAT to verify in plain language (the behaviour or rule under test), NEVER a numbered sequence of taps or clicks — you do not know the exact UI well enough to script it, and a wrong literal instruction is worse than a clear goal. The executor has live access to the real app and will work out how to get there.
5. The 'rationale' field MUST name the specific defect class or risk this test is designed to expose.
5b. 'preconditions' MUST be things the tester can CREATE through the UI in this test's own first steps. NEVER state an environmental assumption the tester can only observe and not establish — the absence of data, data held on another device or account, or a state reached outside this app. If your test needs data to exist, the FIRST STEPS must create it through the UI. A test that depends on an unachievable precondition is abandoned without testing anything, which is worse than no test at all.
6. The 'area' field MUST align with the Exploration Directive — do not default to the easiest area.
7. 'requirement_ids' MUST contain ids copied EXACTLY from the '## Requirements You May Cite' list above. Never invent an id or guess a format. Use [] if none apply.
8. SELF-CONTAINED: assume the app starts EMPTY with no pre-existing data. If the test needs data (an existing record, a populated list), the FIRST steps MUST create it through the UI. Never write a precondition that merely asserts data already exists — the executor cannot conjure it and the run will abort without testing anything. 'preconditions' is for app state you can reach by navigating (e.g. 'app is open'), not for data you did not create.
